topics.title: Find the unknowns: balances and equations

concepts.learning_objective: Find an unknown weight on a balanced scale, including by removing equal weights from both plates.
Frame an equation using a letter-number for an unknown quantity in a balance or pattern problem.
Identify an equation as a statement of equality between two expressions with an LHS and an RHS.

topics.title: Trial and error and the same-operation property

concepts.learning_objective: Solve a simple equation by substituting values until the LHS equals the RHS.
Explain that performing the same operation on both sides keeps an equation true.
Use addition-subtraction and multiplication-division as inverse operations to evaluate expressions.
Move a term to the other side of an equation as its additive inverse.
Remove a factor or divisor from one side by dividing or multiplying the other side.
Solve equations with the unknown on both sides and recognise an equation with no solution.
Use the rule of a pattern to form and solve an equation for a position number.
Model a real-life situation with an equation in one unknown and interpret the solution.
Model a think-of-a-number trick algebraically to recover the starting number.
Check whether a given value is the solution of an equation and write equations with a given solution.
Build chains of equations by the same operation on both sides, all sharing one solution.
Describe a real-life situation that an equation models.

topics.title: Mind the mistake, mend the mistake

concepts.learning_objective: Find errors in signs when terms are moved across the equal sign.
Correct a faulty solution step and find the right value of the unknown.
Recall the origin of bijaganita and the word algebra, and the roles of Brahmagupta and Al-Khwarizmi.
Read an equation written in ancient Indian notation with ya and ru.
Apply Brahmagupta's formula x = (D - B)/(A - C) and solve historical problems.
